hints.title: Recursive Path Multiplication Obstacle
hints.text: The robot can only move right or down at any step. Evaluating every branch recursively leads to redundant calculations of paths from identical cells. How can computing path counts starting from adjacent cells build the answer row by row?

hints.title: Sum of Inward Neighbors Invariant
hints.text: The unique paths to reach cell (r, c) equals the paths to cell (r-1, c) plus the paths to cell (r, c-1), which can be stored in a single 1D row.

hints.title: Single-Row In-Place DP Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a 1D row of size n filled with 1s, since there is only 1 path along any single row. For each remaining row from 1 to m-1, update each column index c from 1 to n-1 by adding the value from column c-1 to the existing value at column c. Return the final element of the row.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Compresses 2D grid DP into a single 1D array of length N.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Uncached recursion branches into two subproblems at every cell, resulting in O(2^(M+N)) time complexity.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A single 1D array of size N reduces auxiliary space from O(M*N) to O(N) while preserving O(M*N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Formulating the recurrence dp[r][c] = dp[r-1][c] + dp[r][c-1] and optimizing space to a 1D rolling array.
